It lets AI assistants read, analyze, create, and update workouts, routines, exercise templates, and body measurements through authenticated Hevy API requests [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/86385d8b-fd28-42af-bebd-e017cd533d92). 6 7 The codebase is a TypeScript monorepo organized as a **private workspace orchestrator** with six packages under `packages/`. The root has no runtime `src/` tree — all implementation lives in the workspaces [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 8 9 The defining architectural property is that a **single MCP tool contract runs identically on two very different runtimes**: 10 11 ```text 12 Hosted: AI assistant → Streamable HTTP → Cloudflare Worker → Hevy API 13 Local: AI assistant → MCP over stdio → local hevy-mcp → Hevy API 14 ``` 15 16 [[3]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/86385d8b-fd28-42af-bebd-e017cd533d92) 17 18 This is achieved by keeping the tool implementations and API client runtime-neutral, then composing them into runtime-specific adapters (Node.js and Cloudflare Workers) that never share code with each other [[4]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). 19 20 The six workspaces and their roles at a glance: 21 22 | Workspace | Package name | Role | 23 | ---------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | 24 | `packages/hevy-client` | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | Runtime-neutral API client (Kubb-generated) | 25 | `packages/operations` | `@hevy-mcp/operations` | Runtime-neutral shared operations layer | 26 | `packages/core` | `@hevy-mcp/core` | Runtime-neutral MCP tools and server construction | 27 | `packages/node` | `hevy-mcp` | Node.js stdio/HTTP adapter — the only publishable workspace | 28 | `packages/worker` | `@hevy-mcp/worker` | Private Cloudflare Worker HTTP/OAuth adapter | 29 | `packages/cli` | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | Public Hevy command-line client | 30 31 [[5]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6) 32 33 ## Workspace Dependency Diagram 34 35 The shipped composition graph flows from the runtime-neutral packages outward to the platform adapters and public CLI [[6]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae): 36 37 ```mermaid 38 graph TD 39 HC["@hevy-mcp/hevy-client
runtime-neutral API client"] 40 OPS["@hevy-mcp/operations
runtime-neutral operations layer"] 41 CORE["@hevy-mcp/core
runtime-neutral MCP tools & server"] 42 NODE["hevy-mcp
Node.js stdio/HTTP adapter"] 43 WORKER["@hevy-mcp/worker
Cloudflare Worker HTTP/OAuth adapter"] 44 CLI["@chrisdoc/hevy-cli
public CLI"] 45 46 HC --> OPS 47 HC --> CORE 48 OPS --> CORE 49 CORE --> NODE 50 CORE --> WORKER 51 CORE --> CLI 52 53 style HC fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 54 style OPS fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 55 style CORE fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 56 style NODE fill:#cce5ff,stroke:#004085 57 style WORKER fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#856404 58 style CLI fill:#cce5ff,stroke:#004085 59 ``` 60 61 **Legend:** Green = runtime-neutral · Blue = Node.js adapter · Amber = Cloudflare adapter 62 63 Key constraints to observe in this diagram [[7]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6): 64 65 - `hevy-client`, `operations`, and `core` are **runtime-neutral**: they contain no Node.js built-ins and no Cloudflare-specific bindings, making them safe to import and execute in either runtime. 66 - `hevy-mcp` (Node) and `@hevy-mcp/worker` (Cloudflare) both consume `core` but **must never import each other**. This boundary is enforced by the `package-boundaries` validation lane [[8]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L209-L227). 67 - `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` bundles the runtime-neutral packages directly and does **not** depend on either adapter. 68 - `@hevy-mcp/core` depends on both `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` and `@hevy-mcp/operations` [[9]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/core/package.json#L20-L24); `@hevy-mcp/operations` depends on `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` [[10]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/operations/package.json#L16-L18). 69 70 > [!IMPORTANT] 71 > The adapter packages (`hevy-mcp` and `@hevy-mcp/worker`) must never import one another. Violating this constraint would pull Node-specific or Cloudflare-specific code into the wrong runtime bundle and cause hard failures at runtime. 72 73 ## Runtime-Neutral vs. Platform Adapters 74 75 ### What "runtime-neutral" means 76 77 A package is **runtime-neutral** when it makes no assumptions about the JavaScript host environment. Concretely, this means: 78 79 - **No Node.js built-ins**: `process`, `fs`, `child_process`, `path`, `crypto` (Node's version), etc. are forbidden. 80 - **No Cloudflare-specific bindings**: KV namespaces, Durable Objects, environment secrets injected via `env` object, and Worker-specific globals are forbidden. 81 - **Standard Web APIs only**: `fetch`, `URL`, `TextEncoder`, `crypto` (Web Crypto), and the rest of the [WinterCG](https://wintercg.org/) baseline. 82 83 The two packages that must satisfy this constraint are `packages/hevy-client` and `packages/core` [[11]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). The `packages/operations` layer also sits in this neutral zone — it depends only on `hevy-client` and adds no platform imports [[10]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/operations/package.json#L16-L18). 84 85 ### The adapter pattern 86 87 Platform-specific concerns are isolated to the adapter packages: 88 89 | Package | Owns | 90 | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 91 | `packages/node` | stdio transport, local Streamable HTTP transport, process lifecycle (`SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`), Node telemetry (Sentry, OTLP), stdio observability, update checks | 92 | `packages/worker` | Cloudflare Worker HTTP entrypoint, Streamable HTTP handler, OAuth 2.1 layer (KV-backed), Cloudflare bindings and environment types | 93 94 [[12]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae) 95 96 ### Enforcement 97 98 The `package-boundaries` lane (blocking, runs on Node 24 and 26) uses dependency-cruiser to statically validate that the boundary rules hold across the entire workspace graph [[8]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L209-L227). A pull request that introduces a Node built-in into `packages/core` or a Cloudflare binding into `packages/hevy-client` will fail CI before merge. 99 100 > [!NOTE] 101 > `packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts` is a deliberate exception: it resides in the Node adapter and instruments private MCP SDK internals. The runtime-neutral packages themselves remain clean; see [Key Design Decisions](#key-design-decisions) for details on the stdio observability tradeoff. 102 103 ## Why This Structure Exists 104 105 ### One tool contract, two runtimes 106 107 The primary motivation is to expose the same 26 MCP tools to users regardless of whether they run the server locally via npm or connect to the hosted Cloudflare endpoint. Splitting implementation into runtime-neutral packages and thin adapters is the only way to achieve this without duplicating logic [[13]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/86385d8b-fd28-42af-bebd-e017cd533d92). 108 109 ### Preventing invalid bundles 110 111 Bundling Node.js code (anything that imports `process`, `fs`, `os`, etc.) into a Cloudflare Worker will fail at deploy time or produce silent runtime errors. Conversely, shipping Cloudflare bindings inside the published npm package would make it non-functional on a developer's machine. The strict layer boundary eliminates both failure modes at the source [[12]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). 112 113 ### Clean published surface 114 115 Only one workspace is publishable to npm: `hevy-mcp` (the Node adapter). Everything else is either a private internal package or a separate public package: 116 117 | Package | Published? | Why | 118 | ----------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------- | 119 | `hevy-mcp` | ✅ npm | The user-facing Node.js MCP server | 120 | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | ✅ npm | Public standalone CLI | 121 | `@hevy-mcp/core` | ❌ private | Internal; bundled into both adapters | 122 | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | ❌ private | Internal; bundled into both adapters | 123 | `@hevy-mcp/operations` | ❌ private | Internal; bundled into both adapters | 124 | `@hevy-mcp/worker` | ❌ private | Deployed directly to Cloudflare Workers | 125 126 [[14]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae) 127 128 ### Private versioning for release/deployment identity 129 130 The private workspaces (`core`, `hevy-client`, `operations`, `worker`) are still versioned using Changesets. This provides internal release and deployment identity — for example, knowing exactly which `@hevy-mcp/core` version is running in production — without ever creating npm tags (`privatePackages.tag=false`) [[14]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). 131 132 > [!NOTE] 133 > Worker deployment happens only when a Changesets version commit changes `packages/worker/package.json`. Public Node or CLI releases do not trigger a Worker deploy; Worker-only private releases still do [[15]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). 134 135 ## Changeset Cascade 136 137 Because the private packages are bundled into the published adapters, a change in a shared package must version-bump every downstream consumer. This "cascade" is enforced by the `package-changesets` CI lane (`npm run check:changeset`), which uses the `release-cascade` comparison from `repository/validation-lanes.json` as its machine-readable source of truth [[16]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L259-L273). 138 139 ### Cascade rules 140 141 ```mermaid 142 flowchart TD 143 Q["Which package did you change?"] 144 145 Q --> HC["@hevy-mcp/hevy-client"] 146 Q --> OPS["@hevy-mcp/operations"] 147 Q --> CORE["@hevy-mcp/core"] 148 Q --> NODE["packages/node
(hevy-mcp)"] 149 Q --> WORKER["packages/worker
OR cloudflare.config.ts"] 150 Q --> CLI["packages/cli
(@chrisdoc/hevy-cli)"] 151 152 HC --> HC_BUMPS["Bump: hevy-client,
operations, core,
hevy-mcp, worker, CLI"] 153 OPS --> OPS_BUMPS["Bump: operations,
core, hevy-mcp,
worker, CLI"] 154 CORE --> CORE_BUMPS["Bump: core,
hevy-mcp, worker, CLI"] 155 NODE --> NODE_BUMPS["Bump: hevy-mcp only"] 156 WORKER --> WORKER_BUMPS["Bump: @hevy-mcp/worker only"] 157 CLI --> CLI_BUMPS["Bump: @chrisdoc/hevy-cli only"] 158 159 style HC_BUMPS fill:#fce4ec 160 style OPS_BUMPS fill:#fce4ec 161 style CORE_BUMPS fill:#fce4ec 162 style NODE_BUMPS fill:#e8f5e9 163 style WORKER_BUMPS fill:#e8f5e9 164 style CLI_BUMPS fill:#e8f5e9 165 ``` 166 167 The full matrix [[17]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae) [[18]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6): 168 169 | Changed package | Required changeset packages | 170 | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 171 | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client`, `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | 172 | `@hevy-mcp/operations` | `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | 173 | `@hevy-mcp/core` | `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | 174 | Node adapter only | `hevy-mcp` only | 175 | Worker only (or `cloudflare.config.ts`) | `@hevy-mcp/worker` only | 176 | CLI only | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` only | 177 178 ### Concrete examples 179 180 | Change | Packages touched | Required changeset packages | 181 | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | 182 | Adding a new MCP tool | `packages/core` | `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | 183 | Fixing a bug in the Hevy client wrapper | `packages/hevy-client` | All six packages | 184 | Updating Worker OAuth logic | `packages/worker` | `@hevy-mcp/worker` only | 185 | Adding a CLI subcommand | `packages/cli` | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` only | 186 | Updating `cloudflare.config.ts` | (root, Worker release trigger) | `@hevy-mcp/worker` only | 187 188 ### How it is enforced 189 190 CI runs `npm run check:changeset` (`npx changeset status --since=origin/`) as a blocking gate on every pull request [[19]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). The `package-changesets` lane checks that every changed workspace directory has a changeset file that names that package, then applies the transitive composition matrix. The `release-cascade` comparison label in `repository/validation-lanes.json` is the machine-readable definition driving this check [[20]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L259-L287). 191 192 > [!IMPORTANT] 193 > The Conventional Commit type (`chore:`, `docs:`, etc.) does **not** determine changeset eligibility. What matters is whether the change touches a file under `packages/*`, modifies runtime-visible behaviour, changes a workspace dependency, or updates an explicit release trigger like `cloudflare.config.ts` [[21]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 194 195 ## Key Design Decisions 196 197 ### Generated API client via Kubb 198 199 The Hevy API client, TypeScript types, and Zod schemas under `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` are produced by [Kubb](https://kubb.dev/) from the Hevy OpenAPI specification [[22]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). The generation pipeline is: 200 201 ```bash 202 npm run openapi # fetch upstream Hevy spec → openapi-spec.json 203 npm run build:client # run Kubb → packages/hevy-client/src/generated/ 204 ``` 205 206 > [!WARNING] 207 > **Never edit files in `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` by hand.** All generated TypeScript errors in that directory are expected and should be ignored. Fixes belong in `scripts/openapi-spec.js` (applied before spec write) so they survive future regenerations [[23]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 208 209 Only the curated package barrels (`@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/types` and `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/schemas`) are the public API of the client package. Generated API functions and `.kubb` internals are private [[24]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 210 211 ### Zod schema inference for type-safe tool parameters 212 213 All MCP tool handlers use **Zod schema inference** via the `InferToolParams` utility from `packages/core/src/utils/tool-helpers.ts`. This eliminates manual type assertions and ensures parameter types always match their validation schemas [[25]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 214 215 ```typescript 216 import type { InferToolParams } from "../utils/tool-helpers.js"; 217 218 const getRoutinesSchema = { 219 page: z.coerce.number().int().gte(1).default(1), 220 pageSize: z.coerce.number().int().gte(1).lte(10).default(5), 221 } as const; 222 223 type GetRoutinesParams = InferToolParams; 224 // ↑ Types are automatically derived — no manual interface needed 225 ``` 226 227 See [TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md](./TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md) for the complete pattern, including `createTypedToolHandler` and response-formatter co-location rules. 228 229 > [!NOTE] 230 > Never use `args as { ... }` type assertions, `Record` in handler signatures, or define parameter types separately from their Zod schemas. These patterns break the single-source-of-truth contract and defeat compile-time safety [[26]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc…3173 tokens truncated…d864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L468-L470): 76 77 - Access tokens: **7 days** 78 - Refresh tokens: **30 days** 79 80 These durations reduce KV writes from frequent hourly refreshes while preserving automatic refresh for supported clients [[16]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L468-L470). 81 82 > [!NOTE] 83 > OAuth is purely additive—direct `Authorization: Bearer ` requests keep working unchanged [[17]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L463-L465). The Worker routes bearer values matching the OAuth access-token shape (`userId:grantId:secret`) to the OAuth layer; Hevy API keys never contain a colon, so they continue using the direct Bearer path [[18]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/worker/src/worker-oauth.ts#L67-L74). 84 85 > [!WARNING] 86 > Rotating your Hevy API key invalidates every OAuth grant created with it [[19]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L465-L466). 87 88 To use OAuth with Claude.ai, add the Worker URL ending in `/mcp` as a Claude.ai custom connector and complete the authorization flow in the browser [[20]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L462-L463). 89 90 ### Origin Allowlist 91 92 Browser requests must send an exact origin from the Worker's default allowlist [[21]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/CONTRIBUTING.md#L356-L367): 93 94 - `https://claude.ai` 95 - `https://www.claude.ai` 96 - `https://claude.com` 97 - `https://www.claude.com` 98 - `https://chatgpt.com` 99 - `https://chat.openai.com` 100 - `https://vscode.dev` 101 - `https://github.dev` 102 103 Self-hosted deployments can replace this list with the optional comma-separated Worker variable `MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` [[22]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/CONTRIBUTING.md#L369-L374): 104 105 ```text 106 MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://app.example.com,https://admin.example.com 107 ``` 108 109 Wildcards are unsupported; browser requests with an unmatched `Origin` receive `403` [[23]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/CONTRIBUTING.md#L382-L384). Non-browser requests without an `Origin` header remain accepted [[24]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/CONTRIBUTING.md#L383-L384). 110 111 ### Self-Hosting 112 113 A clean clone can deploy the portable TypeScript Wrangler configuration with [[25]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L479-L480) [[26]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/CONTRIBUTING.md#L298-L312): 114 115 ```bash 116 npx wrangler deploy --x-new-config 117 ``` 118 119 This command deploys to a `workers.dev` URL [[27]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L480-L481). 120 121 **OAuth requires your own `OAUTH_KV` namespace** [[28]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L481): 122 123 ```bash 124 npx wrangler kv namespace create OAUTH_KV 125 ``` 126 127 Bind the namespace ID as `OAUTH_KV` in your Wrangler environment [[29]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/CONTRIBUTING.md#L391-L400). 128 129 Custom domains, routes, and observability destinations are optional account-owned settings [[30]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L481-L482). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cloudflare-worker-development) [[31]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/CONTRIBUTING.md#L282-L355) for full setup details and the distinction between self-hosting and the maintainer-only named environments. 130 131 > [!NOTE] 132 > The Worker does **not** expose legacy SSE or a `GET` event stream [[32]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L472-L475). Clients that rely on SSE must use one of the local Node modes instead. 133 134 ## Local Node stdio Mode (Default) 135 136 The default deployment mode requires no flags — just `npx hevy-mcp` [[33]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L251-L261). Your MCP client spawns hevy-mcp as a child process and communicates over stdin and stdout using the MCP JSON-RPC protocol. This mode is stateful: the server maintains a persistent session for the lifetime of the process [[34]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/CONTRIBUTING.md#L55-L75). 137 138 `npx` requires Node.js 20 or newer [[35]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L260-L261). 139 140 ### Authentication 141 142 The `HEVY_API_KEY` is injected through the child process environment [[36]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L492-L494). The key never appears in a network header from the client side — the MCP client passes it to the spawned hevy-mcp process, which uses it internally when calling the Hevy API. 143 144 ### Client Configuration 145 146 Client configuration varies by platform. Each example shows the config file path and the JSON block or command needed to connect to hevy-mcp in stdio mode. 147 148 #### Claude Desktop 149 150 **macOS:** `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` 151 **Windows:** `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` 152 153 ```json 154 { 155 "mcpServers": { 156 "hevy": { 157 "command": "npx", 158 "args": ["-y", "hevy-mcp"], 159 "env": { 160 "HEVY_API_KEY": "your-hevy-api-key" 161 } 162 } 163 } 164 } 165 ``` 166 167 [[37]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L172-L188) [[38]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L241-L249) 168 169 #### Cursor 170 171 **Location:** `~/.cursor/mcp.json` 172 173 Use the same JSON block as Claude Desktop above. 174 175 #### Codex 176 177 ```bash 178 codex mcp add hevy \ 179 --env HEVY_API_KEY=your-hevy-api-key \ 180 -- npx -y hevy-mcp 181 ``` 182 183 [[39]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L164-L170) 184 185 #### Docker (stdio mode) 186 187 Docker stdio mode requires the `-i` flag to keep stdin open: 188 189 ```bash 190 export HEVY_API_KEY=your-hevy-api-key 191 docker run -i --rm -e HEVY_API_KEY ghcr.io/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp:latest 192 ``` 193 194 For MCP client configuration with Docker, use an env-file approach: 195 196 ```json 197 { 198 "mcpServers": { 199 "hevy": { 200 "command": "docker", 201 "args": [ 202 "run", 203 "-i", 204 "--rm", 205 "--env-file", 206 "/absolute/path/to/hevy-mcp.env", 207 "ghcr.io/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp:latest" 208 ] 209 } 210 } 211 } 212 ``` 213 214 [[40]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L284-L319) 215 216 > [!TIP] 217 > **bunx alternative** (requires [Bun](https://bun.sh/)): 218 > 219 > ```json 220 > { 221 > "mcpServers": { 222 > "hevy": { 223 > "command": "bunx", 224 > "args": ["hevy-mcp@latest"], 225 > "env": { 226 > "HEVY_API_KEY": "your-hevy-api-key" 227 > } 228 > } 229 > } 230 > } 231 > ``` 232 233 ### Debug and Telemetry 234 235 Set `HEVY_MCP_DEBUG=1` (exactly `1`) for privacy-bounded diagnostics [[41]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L496). Debug output is written to stderr; stdout is reserved exclusively for MCP JSON-RPC messages [[41]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L496). 236 237 > [!NOTE] 238 > stdout remains reserved for MCP JSON-RPC. All debug output goes to stderr to avoid interfering with the protocol. 239 240 Telemetry is enabled by default. Set `HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY=0` (exactly `0`) before startup or import to disable all project telemetry, including Sentry error reporting and OTLP traces/metrics [[42]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L498). 241 242 The update check cache is stored at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/hevy-mcp/update-check.json`, defaulting to `~/.cache/hevy-mcp/update-check.json` when `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is unset [[43]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L499). 243 244 ## Local Node HTTP Mode 245 246 The local Node executable uses stdio by default. Opt into local HTTP mode with the `--transport http --host --port ` flags [[44]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L505-L506). This mode is distinct from the stateless Cloudflare Worker: the Node server owns stateful client sessions and shares an in-memory cache across concurrent sessions within the same running process [[45]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L521-L523). 247 248 ### Quickstart 249 250 ```bash 251 HEVY_API_KEY=your-hevy-api-key npx hevy-mcp --transport http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3000 252 ``` 253 254 The MCP endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp` [[46]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L508-L512). 255 256 ### Security 257 258 > [!IMPORTANT] 259 > Non-loopback binds require the separate `HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` environment variable [[47]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L512-L513). This token protects the HTTP endpoint itself. 260 261 > [!WARNING] 262 > Never use the Hevy API key as the HTTP bearer token [[48]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L497). The `HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` is a separate security boundary for the HTTP transport layer, while `HEVY_API_KEY` authenticates with the Hevy service. 263 264 Loopback-only binds (127.0.0.1 or localhost) do not require `HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` [[49]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L496-L497). 265 266 ### Docker 267 268 Docker deployments must publish the port explicitly with `-p` and use `--host 0.0.0.0` to bind to all interfaces [[50]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L514-L519): 269 270 ```bash 271 docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 -e HEVY_API_KEY -e HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN \ 272 ghcr.io/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp:latest --transport http --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000 273 ``` 274 275 Because `0.0.0.0` is a non-loopback address, `HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` is required [[47]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L512-L513). 276 277 ### Cache Behavior 278 279 The server maintains a server-scoped in-memory cache for `search-exercise-templates` and `hevy://exercise-templates` [[51]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L527-L534): 280 281 - Entries live for five minutes; the cache holds at most one catalog. 282 - Concurrent catalog requests share an in-flight fetch when possible. 283 - `search-exercise-templates` accepts `refresh: true` to invalidate the cache. 284 - Paginated `get-exercise-templates` calls always fetch their requested page. 285 - Unlike the hosted Worker, which gets a fresh cache per request, the Node server shares the cache across all sessions in the same running process [[52]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L534). 286 287 ## Do I Need OAuth? Decision Tree 288 289 Use this flowchart to decide whether you need OAuth 2.1 or can use a simpler direct bearer configuration. 290 291 ```mermaid 292 flowchart TD 293 A[Start: Need to connect to hevy-mcp?] --> B{Can your client send a fixed\nAuthorization: Bearer header?} 294 B -->|Yes| C[No OAuth needed\nUse direct Bearer with Hevy API key] 295 B -->|No| D{Is your client browser-based?} 296 D -->|"Yes — Claude.ai, ChatGPT, etc."| E[Use hosted Worker with OAuth] 297 D -->|No| F[Consider local stdio mode instead] 298 ``` 299 300 > [!NOTE] 301 > The OAuth layer is **purely additive**. If you can send a fixed `Authorization: Bearer ` header, you never need OAuth — even on the hosted Worker. OAuth exists only for browser-based clients (like Claude.ai custom connectors) that cannot attach fixed headers to outbound requests [[53]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L462-L475). 302 303 ## Authentication Flow Diagrams 304 305 ### Direct Bearer Auth 306 307 The simplest authentication path — works with all three deployment modes [[54]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L430-L448). 308 309 ```mermaid 310 sequenceDiagram 311 participant Client 312 participant Worker/Node 313 participant Hevy API 314 Client->>Worker/Node: Authorization: Bearer 315 Worker/Node->>Hevy API: api-key: 316 Hevy API-->>Worker/Node: Response 317 Worker/Node-->>Client: MCP Response 318 ``` 319 320 > [!IMPORTANT] 321 > The Worker validates the key with Hevy on **each request**, does not store it, and forwards it upstream only as Hevy's required `api-key` header [[6]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L446-L448). 322 323 ### OAuth 2.1 Flow (Hosted Worker only) 324 325 Used by browser-based clients such as Claude.ai custom connectors that cannot send a fixed `Authorization` header. Requires an `OAUTH_KV` binding on the Worker [[55]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/CONTRIBUTING.md#L386-L418). 326 327 ```mermaid 328 sequenceDiagram 329 participant Client 330 participant Worker 331 participant User 332 participant Hevy API 333 Client->>Worker: Request with no auth 334 Worker-->>Client: WWW-Authenticate challenge 335 Client->>Worker: GET /authorize 336 Worker-->>User: Paste your Hevy API key 337 User->>Worker: Submit key 338 Worker->>Hevy API: Validate key 339 Hevy API-->>Worker: Valid 340 Worker-->>Client: Authorization code 341 Client->>Worker: POST /token (PKCE exchange) 342 Worker-->>Client: Access token + refresh token 343 Client->>Worker: Subsequent requests with access token 344 Worker->>Hevy API: api-key: 345 Hevy API-->>Worker: Response 346 Worker-->>Client: MCP Response 347 ``` 348 349 OAuth access tokens last **7 days** and refresh tokens last **30 days** [[16]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L468-L470). Rotating your Hevy API key invalidates every OAuth grant created with it [[56]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L464-L466). 350 351 ## When to Use Each Mode 352 353 | Scenario | Recommended Mode | 354 | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 355 | **I'm using Claude Desktop** | [Local Node stdio](#local-node-stdio-mode-default) — Claude Desktop spawns `npx hevy-mcp` as a child process. No server to manage. | 356 | **I'm using Claude.ai in the browser** | [Hosted Cloudflare Worker](#hosted-cloudflare-worker-mode) — the public Worker at `https://mcp.hevy-mcp.dev/mcp` supports OAuth 2.1, enabling Claude.ai custom connectors without a fixed header. | 357 | **I'm using Cursor** | [Local Node stdio](#local-node-stdio-mode-default) — add the `mcpServers` entry to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. | 358 | **I'm using Codex** | Either mode works. Use the hosted endpoint for zero local setup (`codex mcp add hevy --url ... --bearer-token-env-var HEVY_API_KEY`) or local stdio for air-gapped use. | 359 | **I want to share access with my team** | [Hosted Cloudflare Worker](#hosted-cloudflare-worker-mode) — use the public endpoint or self-host your own Worker via `npx wrangler deploy --x-new-config`. | 360 | **I'm running in Docker** | [Local Node HTTP](#local-node-http-mode) — publish the port explicitly and use `--host 0.0.0.0`. See the Docker example in that section. | 361 | **I'm developing or testing locally** | [Local Node stdio](#local-node-stdio-mode-default) or [Local Node HTTP](#local-node-http-mode) — stdio is simpler; HTTP mode is useful when you need an HTTP endpoint for testing or a non-stdio client. | 362 | **I need zero local installs** | [Hosted Cloudflare Worker](#hosted-cloudflare-worker-mode) — no Node.js, Docker, or package download required [[57]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L74-L78). | 363 364 ## Related Documentation 365 366 - **[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)** — Cloudflare Worker development, self-hosting setup, OAuth/KV namespace configuration, and origin allowlist customization [[58]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/CONTRIBUTING.md#L282-L425). 367 - **[README.md](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/main/README.md)** — full client configuration examples for Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, Google Antigravity, Docker, and other MCP clients [[59]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/README.md#L159-L327).

   417	| `HEVY_MCP_API_TIMEOUT`           | `30000` ms                       | Local stdio                   | Positive Hevy API timeout in milliseconds. Invalid values fall back to 30 seconds.                                                           |
   418	| `HEVY_MCP_DEBUG`                 | Disabled                         | Local Node                    | Set to exactly `1` for privacy-bounded diagnostics on stderr. Stdout remains reserved for MCP JSON-RPC.                                      |
   419	| `HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN`     | None                             | Non-loopback HTTP             | Required when `--host` is not loopback; use a separate token, never the Hevy API key.                                                        |
   420	| `HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY`             | Enabled                          | Local Node                    | Set to exactly `0` before startup/import to disable Sentry and OTLP telemetry. Takes precedence over packaged/runtime collector credentials. |
   421	| `HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY_DIAGNOSTICS` | Enabled                          | Local Node                    | Set to exactly `0` to keep structural telemetry while suppressing exception messages and stacks.                                             |
   422	| `XDG_CACHE_HOME`                 | `~/.cache`                       | Local stdio                   | Changes the root for the npm update-check cache at `hevy-mcp/update-check.json`.                                                             |
   423	| `SENTRY_DSN`                     | Packaged Sentry SaaS project DSN | Optional local Node telemetry | Sentry project DSN override. An empty value disables Sentry export. The Worker does not import Node telemetry.                               |
   424	| `SENTRY_RELEASE`                 | `hevy-mcp@<installed-version>`   | Optional local Node telemetry | Overrides the release label attached to local Sentry error events.                                                                           |
   425	| `-h`, `--help`                   | N/A                              | Local stdio CLI               | Print supported options and exit.                                                                                                            |
   426	| `-v`, `--version`                | N/A                              | Local stdio CLI               | Print the installed version and exit.                                                                                                        |
   427	
   428	The local executable uses stdio by default. To opt into Streamable HTTP, run:
   429	
   430	```bash
   431	HEVY_API_KEY=your-hevy-api-key npx hevy-mcp --transport http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3000
   432	```
   433	
   434	The MCP endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp`. For a specific bind host,
   435	HTTP mode validates the Host header and configured port to protect against DNS
   436	rebinding. Loopback is the default. Wildcard binds (`0.0.0.0` or `::`) accept
   437	any hostname so they can be used behind Docker port mappings or a reverse
   438	proxy; they require `HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` and rely on that separate
   439	authentication token. Do not expose an unprotected shared Hevy account to the
   440	public internet. For Docker HTTP mode, publish the port explicitly:
   441	
   442	```bash
   443	docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 -e HEVY_API_KEY -e HEVY_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN \
   444	  ghcr.io/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp:latest --transport http --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000
   445	```
   446	
   447	Wildcard binds are allowed only with the separate bearer token; publish the
   448	container port deliberately and keep that token private.
   449	
   450	### Cache behavior
   451	
   452	`search-exercise-templates` and `hevy://exercise-templates` share a
   453	server-scoped in-memory catalog cache:
   454	
   455	- Entries live for five minutes, and the cache holds at most one catalog.
   456	- Concurrent catalog requests share an in-flight fetch when possible.
   457	- `search-exercise-templates` accepts `refresh: true` to invalidate the cache.
   458	- Each hosted Worker request gets a fresh cache, preventing cross-key sharing.
   459	
   460	### Local Node telemetry and privacy
   461	
   462	The local Node package enables project telemetry by default. It is local Node
   463	behavior only; the Cloudflare Worker does not import Node telemetry. Set
   464	`HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY=0` before startup or import to disable all project
   465	telemetry. Only the literal value `0` opts out: an unset value, an empty value,
   466	`1`, `false`, and every other value remain enabled. The master setting takes
   467	precedence over `SENTRY_DSN` and packaged or runtime `OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN`
   468	credentials, so the disabled path creates no telemetry exporters or periodic
   469	metric readers and makes no telemetry network requests. `SENTRY_DSN` remains a
   470	Sentry-only setting; when telemetry is enabled, an empty value disables only
   471	Sentry export.
   472	
   473	When enabled, actionable errors are sent to the Sentry project configured by
   474	`SENTRY_DSN`; Sentry performance tracing is disabled. Exception messages and
   475	stacks are bounded and scrubbed before export. Set
   195	## Key Design Decisions
   196	
   197	### Generated API client via Kubb
   198	
   199	The Hevy API client, TypeScript types, and Zod schemas under `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` are produced by [Kubb](https://kubb.dev/) from the Hevy OpenAPI specification [[22]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). The generation pipeline is:
   200	
   201	```bash
   202	npm run openapi       # fetch upstream Hevy spec → openapi-spec.json
   203	npm run build:client  # run Kubb → packages/hevy-client/src/generated/
   204	```
   205	
   206	> [!WARNING]
   207	> **Never edit files in `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` by hand.** All generated TypeScript errors in that directory are expected and should be ignored. Fixes belong in `scripts/openapi-spec.js` (applied before spec write) so they survive future regenerations [[23]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6).
   208	
   209	Only the curated package barrels (`@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/types` and `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/schemas`) are the public API of the client package. Generated API functions and `.kubb` internals are private [[24]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6).
   210	
   211	### Zod schema inference for type-safe tool parameters
   212	
   213	All MCP tool handlers use **Zod schema inference** via the `InferToolParams` utility from `packages/core/src/utils/tool-helpers.ts`. This eliminates manual type assertions and ensures parameter types always match their validation schemas [[25]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6).
   214	
   215	```typescript
   216	import type { InferToolParams } from "../utils/tool-helpers.js";
   217	
   218	const getRoutinesSchema = {
   219		page: z.coerce.number().int().gte(1).default(1),
   220		pageSize: z.coerce.number().int().gte(1).lte(10).default(5),
   221	} as const;
   222	
   223	type GetRoutinesParams = InferToolParams<typeof getRoutinesSchema>;
   224	// ↑ Types are automatically derived — no manual interface needed
   225	```
   226	
   227	See [TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md](./TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md) for the complete pattern, including `createTypedToolHandler` and response-formatter co-location rules.
   228	
   229	> [!NOTE]
   230	> Never use `args as { ... }` type assertions, `Record<string, unknown>` in handler signatures, or define parameter types separately from their Zod schemas. These patterns break the single-source-of-truth contract and defeat compile-time safety [[26]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6).
   231	
   232	### Centralized error handling via `withErrorHandling`
   233	
   234	Every MCP tool handler is wrapped with `withErrorHandling` from `packages/core/src/utils/error-handler.ts`. This utility:
   235	
   236	- Catches all handler errors and converts them to standardized `isError: true` MCP responses.
   237	- Preserves the full TypeScript parameter types of the wrapped function.
   238	- Attaches a `context` string used in error diagnostics.
   239	
   240	```typescript
   241	server.registerTool(
   242		"get-routines",
   243		{ description: "...", inputSchema: z.object(getRoutinesSchema) },
   244		withErrorHandling(async (args: GetRoutinesParams) => {
   245			// handler body
   246		}, "get-routines"),
   247	);
   248	```
   249	
   250	[[27]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6)
   251	
   252	### MCP SDK internals dependency for stdio observability
   253	
   254	`packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts` instruments **private MCP SDK stdio fields** to provide raw chunk observability that is not exposed through the SDK's public API [[28]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae):
   255	
   256	- `_ondata` — wrapped to capture incoming chunk byte length and BOM detection before forwarding.
   257	- `_readBuffer` — accessed to replace `readMessage` with an instrumented parser hook.
   258	- `_buffer` — read and rewritten during newline-delimited message extraction.
   259	
   260	[[29]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts#L41-L67)
   261	
   262	The adapter is **fail-closed**: if the private fields are absent (e.g., after an SDK refactor), instrumentation is silently skipped and the original transport is returned unchanged [[30]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts#L86-L90).
   263	
   264	> [!WARNING]
   265	> This is a deliberate architectural tradeoff: private SDK field access provides critical stdio observability that cannot be obtained otherwise, but it means SDK upgrades need careful testing. **Always re-run the complete stdio observability test suite (`npm run test:stdio`) after every MCP TypeScript SDK package upgrade** and inspect the SDK compatibility assumptions before merging [[31]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae).
   266	
   267	## Related Documentation

text(await tools.send_message({target:"/root",message:"Read-only exploration of clean /root/hevy-mcp main (2443cad) complete; no CONTEXT.md or ADRs found, worktree clean. Evidence-backed ranked deepening candidates (no concrete TS interfaces proposed):

1) Deep runtime-neutral MCP application/request host (strongest). `packages/core/src/server.ts:20-75` currently creates `McpServer`, client, catalog, `ToolRuntime`, and registers tools/prompts/resources, but accepts a broad options bag (`createClient`, observer/cache hooks, `decorateServer`, registration callback, timeout/deadline/lifecycle signal). Node repeats composition/lifecycle/telemetry in `packages/node/src/index.ts:247-301,414-497`; Worker repeats default server/transport/client composition in `packages/worker/src/worker.ts:208-244,323-352`. Both adapters have their own validation, deadline, connect, error, and cleanup paths. A deep application host could own server construction + request-scoped execution/cache identity while adapters retain only host-specific auth/transport/lifecycle. Preserve real stateless Worker vs stateful Node HTTP vs stdio differences. Deletion test: remove Node `buildServer`/Worker `createDefaultServer`+`serveMcpRequest` composition duplication while each transport still owns connect/handle/close.

2) Runtime-parity observability seam (strong). Core already has privacy-safe observer contract `packages/core/src/observation.ts:53-127` and cache observer `packages/core/src/utils/cache.ts:10-32`; client exposes request hooks `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client-kubb.ts:76-128`. Node wires OTel/Sentry tool+cache+client observers in `packages/node/src/index.ts:264-277`, `packages/node/src/utils/tool-observer.ts:202-323`, `packages/node/src/utils/hevy-client-observability.ts:105-222`, plus SDK/private transport instrumentation. Worker’s default path (`worker.ts:220-225,228-244,323-350`) only passes `onLog`; no ToolObserver, CacheObserver, onRequestStart/onRequestComplete/onRetryWait, or SDK failure tracking. It does emit structured console events (`worker.ts:246-267,550-555`) and Cloudflare observability is enabled in `cloudflare.config.ts:20-53`, so the gap is application-level tool/API/cache correlation and failure parity, not “no Worker observability.” Deepen a runtime-specific telemetry adapter over the existing neutral events, using Cloudflare-native sinks rather than importing Node OTel. Deletion test: Worker can provide the same bounded event vocabulary without changing core or pulling Node packages.

3) Transport/protocol lifecycle seam (strong, but keep security local). Node HTTP module `packages/node/src/utils/streamable-http.ts` is 494 LOC and owns host validation, body limits, separate HTTP bearer auth, stateful session map, response tracking, disconnect abort, server/transport cleanup (`:23-45,92-220,231-494`). Worker `worker.ts:323-352` creates a fresh Web-standard transport/server per request and handles transport errors. Node stdio adds private SDK internals in `packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts:58-133,347-360`; Node SDK request-handler monkey-patching is in `packages/node/src/utils/sdk-observability.ts:114-300`; Worker has none. A deep protocol-host seam can isolate SDK-version details and common connect/close/error projection while leaving stateful/stateless transport implementations and auth/CORS in their adapters. Deletion test: remove duplicated `server.connect`/transport error/cleanup plumbing without forcing Worker sessions or Node sessions to share semantics.

4) API-key validation and execution-policy module (medium). Node startup probe `packages/node/src/index.ts:215-245` (one static env key; 401/403 -> startup error, network -> warning) and Worker per-request validation `packages/worker/src/worker.ts:292-320,389-429` (deadline-limited, 401/403 -> 401, upstream -> 502) duplicate upstream probe/classification; OAuth calls same Worker validator (`packages/worker/src/worker-oauth.ts:358-417,461-489`). Worker response status/outcome mapping is separate in `packages/worker/src/execution-response.ts:8-47`, while core owns projections (`packages/core/src/execution.ts:15-67`). Centralize only neutral validation/result/deadline classification; keep trust models adapter-local (Node env/static vs Worker bearer/OAuth and separate Node HTTP bearer). Deletion test: no repeated 401/403/deadline mapping, while no adapter shares the other’s credential storage/auth assumptions.

5) Re-evaluate `operations` depth (medium/high maintainability, not primarily transport). `packages/operations/src/index.ts:18-29` exposes only `workouts.list`; implementation is 101 LOC (`workouts.ts:10-101`). Most core tools still call `runtime.getClient()` directly (`packages/core/src/tools/workouts.ts:88-220`, `routines.ts`, `workflows.ts:158-260`, `routine-discovery.ts:21-70`, resources `packages/core/src/resources/hevy.ts:50-129`); CLI uses operations only for workouts list and direct client for remaining commands (`packages/cli/src/commands/index.ts:97-270`). This is either a shallow module to deepen into a coherent domain-operation layer (pagination, expected-404, workflows) or delete. Deletion test: deleting `operations` requires only direct client paths; deepening should remove repeated pagination/404 policy from core/CLI rather than layering wrappers.

6) Execution-context propagation seam (medium, high leverage). `packages/core/src/execution.ts:70-133` maintains a hand-updated `HEVY_CLIENT_OPTION_INDEXES` table and Proxy to inject signal/deadline into every curated client method; tests enumerate every method (`packages/core/src/execution.test.ts:9-93`). `ToolRuntime.forExecution` recursively rebuilds runtime and rebinds client (`packages/core/src/tools/tool-runtime.ts:163-295`); resources manually scope each MCP request (`packages/core/src/resources/hevy.ts:74-127`). Node and Worker both pass lifecycle/deadline through their server factories (`index.ts:264-276`, `worker.ts:228-237,331-336`). A deeper request execution module could make one request scope the leverage point and eliminate brittle option-slot bookkeeping; preserve neutral client semantics. Deletion test: adding/removing a client operation should not require synchronizing an index table across runtime and tests.

Contradictory/stale docs observed: `CONTRIBUTING.md:71-74` still says Node is stdio-only/no `--transport`, while actual `packages/node/src/index.ts:414-497` and `packages/node/src/utils/arguments.ts:61-110` support HTTP. README claims local Node HTTP shares an in-memory catalog across concurrent sessions (`packages/node/README.md:244-285`), but `streamable-http.ts:368-410` calls the server factory per initialize and `index.ts:452-462` builds a fresh server/catalog per session; likely per-session caches. `docs/architecture.md` also has stale 26-tool count. Treat as verification/documentation-locality issue, not proof of runtime bug.

Uncertainty: Cloudflare’s configured `observability` may capture platform traces/logs, but Worker code has no explicit application ToolObserver/client hooks; exact parity depends on destination behavior. Core’s broad options are intentionally runtime-neutral today, so narrowing them would be an architectural tradeoff, not an obvious defect."}));
